metadata.title: आदिवासी विरासत बनाम मुल्क की सियासत | Tribal village where borders blur but identities remain strong
metadata.description:
India’s decision to fence the India-Myanmar border and end the Free Movement Regime (FMR) has sparked deep concerns among the Konyak Naga people of Longwa, a village uniquely positioned on both sides of the international border. For centuries, the people here have lived, farmed, and moved freely between what are now two separate nations. But with the proposed fence, that way of life is under threat.

In this exclusive ground report, we bring you the worries of Longwa’s village elders, farmers, and families, who now face an uncertain future. Many question how they will cultivate their ancestral lands or visit their relatives if a physical barrier divides them. Others worry about the cultural and emotional impact of being severed from their history.
